defects.description: cancel_signal matches a GameState to its MarketMaps only by exact event_key, and event_key embeds the kickoff UTC date. If ESPN reports a kickoff moved to a different UTC date, the state gets a new key and no signal fires, even when the status is in_progress before the mapped start. Probe: the start moved 24h earlier gives event_key E0:arsenal:leeds:2026-10-09, and cancel_signal returns None for both 'scheduled' and 'in_progress'. A 3h move on the same date fires correctly. The WS receive-date key (already noted by the builder) is the same class of gap. Exposure is limited by rarity, the start-5min GTD expiry and remapping.
defects.fix_hint: Select maps by (league, norm_team(home), norm_team(away)) with a start within a few days, instead of exact event_key equality. Add one test with the start moved to the previous day.

defects.description: parse_espn falls back to the coarse ESPN state for an unknown status name: 'pre' -> scheduled, 'post' -> final. So a new halt-type status, for example STATUS_TBD with state pre or a forfeit with state post, would not trigger a cancel. The code comment says unknown statuses fail closed, but that only holds when the state is also unknown.
defects.fix_hint: Fall back to the state only for 'in'. Map any other unknown name to 'suspended', or correct the comment.

defects.description: sgo_snapshots and oddsapi_snapshots default to quota=None, which means no quota check at all. A wiring that forgets to pass a Quota bypasses the 80%/100% fail-closed book for the keyed sources.
defects.fix_hint: Default the quota to Quota() (data/sports/quota.json), so callers have to opt out explicitly.

rules_check: Paper and no auth: odds.py makes only GETs: Kalshi public, ESPN public, the public Polymarket sports WS, and SGO/odds-api only when an env key is present, and none exists. There is no POST, signing or order submission anywhere. gamestate.cancel_game only calls router.cancel through the Router protocol and is tested on a FakeRouter whose submit raises. No LLM or vendor calls. Credentials: env only, read when the call is made (_keyed), and never written: headers are not stored, apiKey is dropped from params, and the line and errors are scrubbed. A grep for secrets over the owned paths and data/sports found nothing, and the raw files contain no apiKey or X-Api-Key. Tests: no network (guard verified effective against httpx and websockets); they write only to tmp_path (data/sports and report hashes unchanged after the run). No look-ahead: football-data closes are CLV only, with obs=kickoff. No sizing code. Results are not fabricated: the smoke report numbers and the quota report reproduce exactly from raw data and the parquet. Owned paths: the builder's files_changed (sports/odds.py, sports/gamestate.py, tests/phase4/test_sports_data.py, reports/phase4_quota.md), plus the fixtures, the smoke report and data/sports/raw, are all inside WP4-A's paths. No other code imports WP4-A modules; sports/pulls.py (WP4-B) only reads the 'sports' feed key. Contracts: trader/contracts.py sha256 1c0e3f29...68bf equals the hash recorded in the Phase 1 audits; the mtimes of advisor/contracts.py (14:21:48, dispatch setup) and common.py (2026-09-30) predate the WP4-A edits. Both reports end with 'How to reproduce'. Minimal code: two modules (482 and 210 lines) and one test file, no speculative abstractions. The ponytail comments mark known ceilings (no lock on the quota file, SGO charging `limit` up front, Kalshi occurrence-3h, the WS receive-date key).

Verified independently, beyond the builder's claims:

Wiring cautions, outside WP4-A's scope:
1. The stale trigger in cancel_signal only works if the loop re-checks the last stored state for each mapped event on a timer. Called only 'on every GameState update', as the dispatch and wiring notes say, recv_ms always equals now, so the stale trigger never fires. Feed-level staleness is still covered by 'sports' in feed_age_ms and pulls.py.
2. http_get uses follow_redirects=True. httpx strips only Authorization on a cross-origin redirect, so a vendor redirect would forward the SGO X-Api-Key header. Consider follow_redirects=False for keyed calls.
3. sgo_snapshots charges `limit` units per call. If the recorder calls it once per due label, usage will far exceed the 3-units-per-event projection. This fails closed, but it wastes quota.
4. The Polymarket WS soccer league codes (epl/lal/bun/sea/fl1) have not been seen live yet; ESPN covers game state in the meantime.

How I ran pytest: with -p no:cacheprovider and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, so the code base was not touched.
